text:
rachel: hi all, newbie question — I rotated my hosted API key earlier and now my local dev scripts are 401ing. Should I be using hosted keys locally at all?

sam: generally no. Use a sandbox key for day-to-day dev. Hosted keys are for staging/prod only. Sandbox keys are lower quota and non-billable for quick experiments.

rachel: where do I get a sandbox key? I only see a "Hosted API Key" button in the console.

devon: Console -> API keys -> Create sandbox key. If you don't see it, you might be missing a permission or the UI is slow after SSO. Ping infra if it's not there.

rachel: got it. created one. But I'm still hitting 429s when running a batch of tests. Any recommended patterns for avoiding rate limits during onboarding?

sam: a few things: 1) add local throttling / sleep between requests during rapid iterate; 2) exponential backoff on 429 using Retry-After header; 3) mock network calls for unit tests; 4) request a small CI sandbox quota for integration tests.

devon: to request CI quota, open a post in #devex with repo name, expected RPS/QPS, and whether it's for CI or staging. For urgent onboarding requests, tag @devon or @infra.

infra-bot: :warning: Security reminder: do not commit hosted keys. If a hosted key is accidentally pushed, rotate immediately and file a security incident.

rachel: also curious about key rotation for services — what's the right sequence? I rotated the token in the console but forgot to update the secret in our CI store and got 401s.

sam: update the key in Console, then update the secret store (Vault/GH Actions secrets), then restart any services/containers that read the secret on startup. If your service caches the key, ensure it reloads secrets or gets restarted.

devon: and double-check scheduled tasks and background jobs that may use a different secret bucket.

rachel: fixed — updated the secrets store and restarted the worker. all green now. thanks!

sam: short onboarding checklist for keys: 1) use sandbox locally, 2) don't commit keys, 3) secrets store for CI, 4) exponential backoff for 429s, 5) request CI quota via #devex with repo and QPS.

rachel: perfect, saving this. appreciate the help :thumbsup:
